| Relay ticket in the subprotocol (CC-07.3, C11)                   | A browser WebSocket cannot send `Authorization`, so the device bearer buys a `pkeyrt_` ticket (192 random bits) that rides `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`. It is stored only as a peppered hash in the `relay-ticket` single-use kind, lives 60 seconds, is bound to the product, the person and the device, and the upgrade consumes it atomically: one ticket opens one socket, and a replay gets `401 relay_ticket_invalid`. The Worker replaces the client's subprotocol list with the bare `pkey-relay.1` before it forwards, so the ticket value never reaches the room, and it drops `Authorization` and `Cookie`. A ticket in a URL would reach access logs; this one does not.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| What the room trusts (CC-07.3)                                   | The room believes its admission header completely. The upgrade route builds it from the consumed ticket, re-checked against the device's current binding, and from a fresh read of the person's devices (the principal rule), never from the client; a client-supplied admission header is overwritten, and a room reached without one answers 400. Both routes check `launch.relay` themselves, and the room checks it again.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Refusals before the socket (CC-07.3)                             | The product's relay switch (`relay_disabled`), the deployment pause (`relay_paused`) and the product's month ceiling (`relay_quota_exceeded`, scope `product`) are checked at ticket time and again at the upgrade, so a ticket does not outlive them by more than a request. The person's day is metered in the room. The local network is never metered and never touches these routes. A ticket costs one authenticated write, so the ticket route has a bucket of 12 a minute per device and the upgrade route a coarse per-network bucket checked before the ticket is hashed or consumed; both fail closed (`rate_limited`, `Retry-After`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Pause and roster reach open rooms (CC-07.3)                      | The room's alarm (every 60 s while sockets are open) re-reads the launch gate, `cloudConnect.relayPaused` and the person's devices under the same principal rule as admission. Gate off or pause on: LIMIT 4, then every socket closes 4008; the pause ending lets the room admit again. A device that left the roster loses its sockets (4003) and the others hear GONE; a person with no device left has the room deleted. An unreadable read keeps the room open and is retried on the next alarm, and the third in a row closes it. So a pause, or a removal the poke missed, reaches an open socket within one alarm (60 s).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| K_disc in the browser (CC-09, R-6w)                              | The discovery key is stored as raw base64url text in the record `pkey.connect.v1` in same-origin IndexedDB, with the roster and certificate: the same standing as the device token, so script on the origin (XSS) can read it and a user of the shared browser profile can too. It is never in a return value, error or print, and `leave()` (sign-out, deactivation) clears it. Tabs of one app share the record under a Web Lock; a lower epoch never replaces a stored one and a stale mark is never cleared by a push.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Metering bounds (CC-07.3)                                        | A room adds its bytes to the day's counter from its alarm, and an alarm that failed after the write may add again on retry: the counter can be over-counted, never under-counted. The product's month total lags by up to (active rooms × 60 s of traffic), because it is read at ticket time and on each alarm. The day quota follows the person's latest admission with `dayUsed` persisted, so a later admission cannot raise what was already spent and nothing exceeds the person's highest entitlement.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Purge and reconnect (CC-07.3)                                    | A purge leaves a tombstone (`erasedAt`) that refuses admissions for 10 minutes, so a reconnect racing an erasure cannot re-create the room.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| The defaults (CC-07.3)                                           | `cloudConnect.relayPaused` defaults to off. `launch.relay` (default off, set at runtime in production) is the single default lock: with it off, both routes and the room answer not-found.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Immediate roster moves (CC-07.4)                                 | When a ring epoch moves, Connect pokes the person's room with the epoch, never a key. The poke is a `PUT` made only through `do/client.ts`; the public upgrade route forwards `GET` only. The room takes only the epoch from it: product and subject must match its pin (403), `launch.relay` is checked again (404 when off), and membership is re-derived from D1 by the admission rule, never from the body. A device that left loses its sockets with 4003 at once, the others hear GONE and then RING; a person with no device left has the room deleted; a poke never creates a room. An unreadable roster closes nothing, RING is still sent and the alarm retries. The poke is best effort (3 s, errors ignored, never fails the write); the 60 s alarm is the backstop. RING carries an epoch only: a client fetches and verifies the roster.                  |
| Hostile peer on the local network (CC-17)                        | A peer needs a certificate signed by the product key and the person's pre-shared key before a channel opens; one without them fails the handshake and learns no identity. Modes `v` and `p` add the code on both screens.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Hostile relay (CC-17)                                            | The relay sees roster membership, sizes and timing, never contents: the Noise channel is end to end between the devices and the relay forwards ciphertext. It cannot add a member, because admission is checked against the roster.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Hostile Worker (CC-17)                                           | See Worker trust in mode `a` above. Contents stay private to the two devices; a Worker that signs a device into a roster is trusted by channels between a person's own devices. Sync keys never cross it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Ticket leak (CC-17)                                              | A `pkeyrt_` ticket lives 60 seconds, opens one socket and is bound to product, person and device. The SDKs send it only to the Worker's host and refuse a redirect of the socket, so a redirected handshake cannot carry it elsewhere.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Redirects (CC-17)                                                | The relay client does not follow a 3xx: the handshake fails and the ticket is not replayed to another host.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| mDNS spoofing and flooding (CC-17)                               | An advert is only a hint: its name is an HMAC under the person's discovery key and nothing in it is trusted until the handshake proves the certificate. Browsing tests at most 512 names per result, and the handshake is limited per advert. The first four addresses learned for a name keep their place: in mode `a` a neighbour that answers first can only deny service, because the handshake authenticates the peer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Global IPv6 address on the LAN (CC-IPV6)                         | A global IPv6 address is dialled or accepted only when it shares the /64 of the socket's own address, outside Teredo and 6to4, and a ULA address must share the /64 of a known local address (`lanVerdict`, V5 §15.4.1). A host off the link cannot finish a TCP handshake with a source on the local /64, because the reply goes on-link; this holds for TCP only and is never reused for UDP. Link-local is on-link by definition, a routed ULA range is not. A source that fails is closed before a slot or a read, even on a `::` listener. Counts key on the full address (4), the /64 (16) and in total (32), with a 30 s bound; a link-local key includes its zone.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| CANDIDATES dial targets (CC-IPV6)                                | A `CANDIDATES` entry comes from a peer that may be compromised. It is dialled only inside a connected subnet of an up, non-tunnel interface, never at one of the device's own addresses, on a port from 1024, in RFC 5952 spelling with no zone, mapped form or `fe80::/10`, and the address text is judged before the connect and the socket before its first byte. A peer cannot steer a receiver at another host or port on a routed RFC 1918 or ULA range, so there is no scan or pivot. An mDNS answer is believed only from a source on the interface's connected subnets (RFC 6762 section 11).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Relay pacing and limits (CC-17)                                  | 200 messages a second per socket with a burst of 400, 2 sockets per device, 32 per room, 64 KiB a frame. A sender over the rate gets `LIMIT` and then a close. The SDKs pace at 180 a second with a burst of 360, halve the rate for 10 seconds on `LIMIT`, and queue at most 8 MiB.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Launch gates for Connect (LG-1)                                  | `launch.connect` serves the identity and devices routes and `launch.relay` serves the relay routes and rooms. Both default off and fail closed; off answers not found and an open room closes within a minute. Turning either on in production is a review trigger (section 9).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Anonymous storefront name, `GET /api/storefront/<slug>` (LK-12d) | Returns `{name, iconUrl}` only for a product Discover offers a new account; every other input gets one uniform 404 with the same body and headers, so "no such product" and "not offered" look alike. Charged to a per-network rate limit before any lookup, which fails closed. Reads no cookie or account. It reveals no more than the public download page does.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

## Platform sign-in (I-13)

A native app trades a Google or Apple ID token from the platform, with a nonce and a proof by the
device's signing key, for a device token (`WIRE-CONTRACT-V5.md` §12.11). It is a second way into
the identity token route, not a second account system. The link offer (I-43) adds a Google or Apple
sign-in method from an app. Rows for nearby approval (I-40) are added with the package that ships it.

| Threat                                     | Control                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Residual                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Token replay and audience confusion (I-13) | Audiences are the product's own (Google `aud` plus `azp`, Apple bundle ids). A card token is refused on the exchange and a native token on the card. The nonce is single use and bound to product, device and signing key, the proof covers the token hash, and `iat` is at most 300 s old.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | A holder of the device's signing key and a fresh token (the device itself).                                                                                                                 |
| Oracle on the exchange (I-13)              | Every verifier, proof, key and nonce failure answers one `400 invalid_grant` with one body. The proof is checked before the nonce is taken, so a caller without the key cannot spend a nonce. Verifier messages are not logged or audited. A provider outage is a separate `503`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | none known                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Takeover by email match (I-13)             | The lookup is `linkedOnly`: by `(issuer, tenant scope, subject)`, it never creates an account and never joins by an email in the token. Apple scopes are bound to the developer's team.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | none                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Consent on a same-device grant (L-1)       | A first or changed scope answers `confirm`, not a token. A narrowed consent is honoured: the token carries only the claims the person granted. The grant is written with the scope hash shown and audited as `signin.consent.granted`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | The app on the device completes the consent call itself. This is inherent to a same-device grant. The app gains what a consented sign-in gives.                                             |
| Device keys written without a bind (I-13)  | Keys are written only after the bind succeeds. The held-key rule and the check that the agreement key is not held by another device run before the bind.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | A race inside one request can leave a bound device with no token until it is replaced.                                                                                                      |
| Agreement key without proof of possession  | The nonce request names the agreement key; it is unique per product within the exchange.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | A key can be registered first by another party, which denies service only.                                                                                                                  |
| The link handle (I-13, I-43.2)             | `exchange-link` holds a verified identity for 600 s under a peppered hash of the handle, bound to product, device and key, and to the subject bound on the device when it was issued. It is consumed only by that key's device, only while the device carries that subject, and only with a step-up. A request that does not match leaves it unspent. It is never logged.                                                                                                                                                  | A handle issued before any sign-in follows the next person to sign in on that device in the same 300 s window; that is the offer's own flow.                                                |
| Step-up mark (I-43.1)                      | `signin-fresh` is written only by same-device grants, and holds the subject that was bound. The link route compares it with the subject bound on the device before it takes the mark, so a different person on the device has no step-up and does not spend it. The exchange, device code, nearby approval and restore never write it.                                                                                                                                                                                     | none                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| App-made link and its scope (I-43.2)       | The link route needs the device bearer, a `link` proof by the device's key, and a live step-up that the request spends. A Google link is global only when the provider vouches for the token's address and the account has already verified it; otherwise it is scoped to the developer. An Apple link is scoped to the team. A scoped link keeps its address unverified. The account's addresses and the linked address are emailed, and the audit row `identity.link.added` carries the kind and reach, never the token. | A developer can link an identity inside its own scope, where it already controls the product.                                                                                               |
| Oracle on the link route (I-43.2)          | Every proof, key, nonce, token and handle-binding failure is one `400 invalid_grant`. Unknown or spent handles answer `404`. The proof is checked before the step-up, the nonce or the handle is touched.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | An unknown handle is distinguishable from a refused one; handles are 256-bit random values.                                                                                                 |
| Shared native audience (I-13.9)            | A developer scope is named by a Google web client id or an Apple team id, so one value is declared by one product. Any other live product that names it is refused at the settings write, at manifest ingest and at resync. No product field proves who the developer is, so there is no same-owner exemption. A sign-in through a scoped link never touches the link's address or its verified flag.                                                                                                                      | A developer cannot share one id across its own products until a verified-ownership model exists. Declarations made before the rule are not rewritten; they are refused at their next write. |
| Device keys and listeners (I-13.9)         | The exchange, `choice/complete` and `PUT /devices/keys` register keys through one Core operation, which raises the `keys` device-change event when the keys changed, so the key ring drops the device's wraps and the Connect roster epoch moves.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | none known                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Consent and the bind (I-13.9)              | `confirm` carries no licence view, so the app learns nothing about the account before consent. The consent row is written right after the bind, in a separate D1 write.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | A failure between the two leaves a bound device whose grant is spent; the person signs in again and is asked again.                                                                         |
| Nonce route and held keys (I-13.9)         | The nonce route answers `400 device_keys_invalid` when the device already holds another signing key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | The answer tells a caller that a 128-bit device id has a different key. Accepted.                                                                                                           |
| Launch gates (LG-1)                        | The platform settings `launch.identityExchange`, `launch.connect`, `launch.syncE2e` and `launch.relay` default off and fail closed: a `[vars]` value of `off` is a hard off and an unreadable store reads off. An off exchange gate answers as before the feature existed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Turning a gate on in production is a review trigger (section 9).                                                                                                                            |

## 8. Out of scope for this model

Physical access to Cloudflare infrastructure; compromise of Cloudflare itself; compromise of the
IdP's own signing keys (we model malicious _claims_, not forged tokens); social engineering of the
operator; and denial of service originating from Cloudflare's own network controls.

## 9. Review triggers

Revisit this document when any of the following changes: a `launch.*` platform setting is added, or its default moves from off or stops failing closed (LG-1); a row joins the GitHub write allow-list, the never-list loses an entry, or a write token is cached or widened beyond one repository; the `distribution:pr` scope joins `DEFAULT_CI_SCOPES` or the exchange takes its repository from the request; a `pkeya_` admin API token gains a scope
(an entry in `ADMIN_API_SCOPES`) or a route row gains a `tokenScope` or `personalToken: true` (the rows an admin `pkeyp_` reaches, A17), which widens a credential
that exists precisely because it is narrower than a session, and A16 stops being true the moment
the scope vocabulary stops being one word; a new tenant that is not first-party is
onboarded; a route writes `licenses.account_id` other than through the compare-and-set claim, an
attach takes its holder from anywhere but the device's sign-in binding, or
`identity.keyEntry.claimByKey` defaults to on (I-09); the portal gains write capability beyond device disconnect and key claim; a second
release channel or artifact type is added; a service gains a route, a table or a secret, or a
descriptor hook gains a method that writes or a new provider, or a method that returns bytes
(today only `releaseCatalog.openSource`); a byte route or a permanent alias is added; edge caching
is turned on for any byte route; a reader of `dist_rollouts` starts deciding what a device is

### The shared assets root and the docs gate (SEC-WEB-1)

**What arrived.** One assets root holds the admin and portal SPA (`/assets/*`, `/manage.html`,
`/index.html`) and the gated docs site (`/docs/**`). The unauthenticated SPA proxies (`/manage/*`
in `console/index.ts`, the portal in `services/identity/portal/index.ts`) used to fetch any
dotted path from that root, so `GET /manage/docs/<file>` served gated docs with no session.

**Control.** `isPublicSpaAssetPath` (`http.ts`) is an allowlist: the proxies fetch only
`/assets/<literal file>`, and every other path is the SPA shell. Docs are served only by
`handleDocs`. Since ST-29 it serves by tier (`DOCS_TIERS`, docs plan §3.1 and D2): the landing
page, the access page, Help (public since DOC-03b), the developer sections, the site's shared
assets and the public search bundle need no session; Operate → Console and its search bundle need
a console member; Operate → Platform, Contribute, the full search bundle and every path no row
names need `can(platform, docs)`. A sessionless request for a gated path is a 302 to
`/docs/access/`, which leaks nothing (the path is not echoed). Search is one Pagefind bundle per
tier (`SEARCH_BUNDLES`, built by `packages/docs/scripts/build-search-bundles.ts`): each holds its
tier's pages and those below it, so no bundle carries text its reader may not open, and a test
reads every fragment of every bundle and fails on a page above the bundle's tier. Gated pages are
`noindex` and out of the sitemap. The gate runs before anything is fetched. Tests:
`test/surfaces/docsGateBypass.test.ts` walks every file in the assembled tree through encoded, cased,
doubled-slash, traversal, HEAD and Range variants: a gated file is denied anonymously by every
route, a public one is served at `/docs` only, and with an admin session every file is served at
`/docs` only; `test/surfaces/docsGate.test.ts` pins the tier table to the docs site's `TIER_PREFIXES` and
the bundle directories to the build's. The docs `check:links` adds the tier rule: a public page's
content links only to public pages (existing exceptions are held in `link-tier-debt.json`, which
only shrinks).

**Docs CSP and WebAssembly.** The docs `script-src` is `'self'`, `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` and the build's
hashes. Pagefind compiles a WebAssembly module, and without the keyword Chromium refuses, so Help and
developer search never returned a result. `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` allows WebAssembly compilation only: it does
not allow `eval`, `new Function` or string timers (that is `'unsafe-eval'`, which never appears), and the
module is a same-origin file the build produced. It is on the docs pages' policy alone, not the admin's.
`test/docsSearchBrowser.test.ts` drives search in Chromium under the Worker's real headers.
**Per-file tiers.** A file under `/docs/_astro/` is public unless the build finds that only gated
pages load it: `collect-docs-tiers.ts` writes those into `docsTiers.generated.ts`
(`DOCS_ASSET_TIERS`, the lowest tier among the pages and files that name it), and `docsTierOf`
serves them at that tier. A moved-page redirect page is served at its target's tier
(`DOCS_REDIRECT_TIERS`), so an old Help link reaches Help. `test/surfaces/docsTiersParity.test.ts` pins both
tables to the built site. The access page carries the wanted page as `returnTo`, which the Worker
puts on the Sign in link only after `sanitizeReturnTo` (a hand-made value falls back to the plain
link); a signed-in reader without the admin area gets the access page's admin wording under a 403.

**The customer host (LK-09).** Help is served at `polaris.locker/docs/help/*` through `handleDocs`,
confined by `customerDocsPath` (Help, `/docs/_astro/`, `/docs/pagefind-help/`, `/docs/branding/`, the
404 page); every other `/docs` path answers a 302 to the console host, and `key.plrs.im/docs/help/*`
a 301 to the customer host. All served paths are public tier; the gate still runs on each.

**Residual.** The docs sidebar is scoped per door in the page (`routeData.ts`), but a public
page's HTML still names only its own door's pages. Anything placed under `/assets/` in the admin
build is public by design. The developer door and Help are public. The search dialog (DOC-02c) loads
exactly one bundle: Help's own on the customer host, else the highest tier `/manage/api/me` says the
session may read (never merged, never a gated bundle without that answer; the gate still runs on
the request). `robots.txt` for the docs host is not served yet, and public HTML is
`no-store`, not cacheable (LK-09).

### The Elements CDN module (UK-04b)

**What arrived.** `GET /elements/<major|version>/<file>` (`core/elements.ts`) serves the built
`@polaris-key/elements` bundle, so any web page can load `<script type="module"
src="https://key.plrs.im/elements/1/pk.js">`. The file runs inside the integrator's page, with the
page's authority: it renders the sign-in, activation and device screens, builds the browser client from
the page's `config`, and handles the person's license key and the session's bearer token. That makes
the bytes this route serves a supply-chain target on par with a package (AT-3).

**Shared origin.** The route lives on the console's origin, which carries the admin cookie
(`__Host-pkey_admin`, R1-08/R1-09). A script served here is never run _by_ this origin's pages, and
the route sets and reads no cookie, touches no database and answers no dynamic content. The assets
layer's `Set-Cookie`, if it ever sent one, is dropped (the response is rebuilt from an allowlist of
headers). `access-control-allow-origin: *` is safe only for that reason: it is never combined with
`Allow-Credentials`, so a foreign page that fetches the file learns nothing it could not `curl`. The
route is on the console host only; the customer host answers it 404 (`CUSTOMER_ROUTE_KINDS`).
The console and docs pages carry `script-src 'self'`, which now admits `/elements/*` as same-origin
script: the module is public, reviewed bytes from the same deploy, not user content, so this adds no
injection path, but it does widen what "same origin" means. Follow-up before 1.0: serve the module
from a cookie-less CDN origin and leave the console CSP untouched; this round does not change it.

**Control: the file set.** Only files `scripts/assemble-assets.mjs` copied from `bundle:cdn` exist
under `assets/elements/`: `pk.js`, content-hashed `chunks/*.js`, `fonts/*`, `integrity.json`. The
path is parsed, never joined: the version segment is a bare major or an exact semver, the file part
matches a conservative character set, `isSafeAssetPath` refuses `.`/`..`, and the extension must be one of
`js`, `css`, `json`, `woff2`, `txt`. Nothing else under the assets root (the admin SPA, `/docs`, the
gated Platform pages) is reachable through it, and a miss is a `404` with `no-store`, never a fallback
to a nearest version. The `elements` product slug is reserved (`RESERVED_PRODUCT_SLUGS`) so no
tenant path can shadow the prefix.

**Control: cache poisoning.** The `Content-Type` comes from the extension, never from the assets
layer, with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; the query string is dropped before the assets
lookup, so `?x=` reaches the same bytes (a shared cache may key on it, which only wastes space, never
changes content); the response carries no `Vary` on a request header, so a shared cache holds one object per
URL; and only a whole `200` is cacheable (an error is `no-store`, so a transient 404 during a deploy is
not remembered by the edge for a year). An exact-version URL is `immutable` for a year: it is safe
because its bytes can never legitimately change, and unsafe the day they do. The bundle is named for
the release: `deploy.yml` passes the tag's version (`PKEY_ELEMENTS_VERSION`) to `assemble`, because
the committed `package.json` says `0.0.0`. `bundle-cdn.mjs` refuses `0.0.0` under `CI` (the test and
assemble jobs opt in with `PKEY_ELEMENTS_UNSTAMPED_OK`), and the route serves an unstamped `0.0.0`
`no-cache`, never immutable. A fix ships as a new version. The floating major follows only stable
tags: a prerelease deploy (`PKEY_ELEMENTS_FLOAT=0`) publishes its exact version and writes no major
shim, so the major URL does not move to a prerelease (it answers 404 until the next stable deploy,
since the assets root holds one build; see Residual 2). `deploy.yml` also fails before the migrations
if a product already uses the slug `elements`. `test/releaseWorkflows.test.ts` pins all three.

**Control: pinning.** Integrators have two tiers. The floating major (`/elements/1/pk.js`,
`max-age=300`) is a one-line shim that re-exports the exact version, so a new release reaches pages
within minutes and the shim never refers to a chunk that was removed; it carries no `integrity` (its
target changes). Pinned pages use `/elements/1.4.2/pk.js` with
`integrity="sha384-…"` from `/elements/1.4.2/integrity.json` (`crossorigin` is implied for module
scripts). A browser verifies the module's hash before running it, but only for the top-level
module: `integrity` on a `<script>` is **not** checked on the modules it imports, and a content-hashed
chunk name is not a check either (reviewer probe: a tampered `chunks/*.js` ran under a valid `pk.js`
hash). Transitive coverage needs an import map: `integrity.json` carries `importMap`, every `.js`
file's sha384 keyed by absolute URL, for `<script type="importmap">{"integrity": {…}}</script>`
placed before the module script (the probe then refuses the tampered chunk). Where the browser lacks
import-map integrity, only `pk.js` is verified (Residual 5). Fonts and `integrity.json` itself are
not covered: fonts are data and the integrity file is a convenience, not a root of trust, so the hash
in the integrator's page comes from the release notes or `pkey`-side tooling, not from a fetch at
load time.

**Residual.** (1) Whoever can deploy the Worker, or alter the `elements` build in CI, can change the
bytes served at the floating major (and at a not-yet-released exact version); a page without
`integrity` trusts that supply chain. This is the same trust as the package feed, no more. (2) Only
the exact versions a deployment was built with exist: the assets root holds the current version, so an
older pinned URL 404s after the next release, a rollback or the redeploy of an older tag (which replaces
the root with that tag's build) until an archive of released versions is added; pinned pages fail
closed, not open. (3) The integrator's own CSP should allow the path, not the host: `script-src
https://key.plrs.im/elements/` and `font-src https://key.plrs.im/elements/`, so no other script on the
console origin is admitted; this route sets no CSP of its own (it serves no document). (4) A
compromised module could read what the page gives the gate (the license key typed into it, the bearer
token) and post it elsewhere; the defence is SRI on an exact version, with the import map so the chunks are covered too, not
anything the route can add. (5) Import-map `integrity` is not supported by every browser (Chrome and
Edge 127 and later; others vary): where it is not, only `pk.js` is verified and a tampered chunk runs.
Tests: `test/elements.test.ts` (paths, headers, 404s, byte stability and integrity of the built
bundle), `test/routeCoverage.test.ts`.
